name: PackStation
idea: Tablet-friendly packing screen that turns any order export into pick lists, per-customer pack checklists and box labels for farms, CSAs and food hubs.
description: Hub operators and small farms import an order CSV from whatever shop tool they use, then get an interactive packing screen: filter by storage type (frozen, chilled, dry), customer, producer and pick-up versus delivery, tick items off as packed, and print labels. No payments are handled. Hard part is the per-platform CSV importers and an offline-first sync so it keeps working in a warehouse with bad wifi.
web_delivery: PWA with IndexedDB offline storage and Supabase sync; CSV parsing and label printing done client-side on Vercel hobby.
why_hard_to_copy: Needs offline-first sync plus a library of messy export formats from several farm and food-hub platforms; generic CRUD clones will not cover those.

signals.summary: A hub operator moving from another platform relies on a digital warehouse packing workflow; the thread asks for a tablet packing screen with filters by storage type, customer, producer and packed status to replace static packing reports.
Wholesale flower hubs say shopping is so brisk when the store opens that buyers miss out; hub managers are burdened by manually entering pre-orders made outside the platform.

name: GedFix
idea: Client-side GEDCOM checker and upgrader that reads messy 5.5.1 exports and produces clean GEDCOM 7 without uploading the family tree anywhere.
description: Genealogists paste or drop a .ged file and get a report of structural problems, a plain-language fix list, and a converted GEDCOM 7 file, all inside the browser so private family data never leaves the device. Targets exports from Family Tree Maker, RootsMagic, Ancestry and others, which each bend the standard differently. Hard to copy because correctness depends on many vendor quirks and the GEDCOM 7 spec.
web_delivery: Static web app with a parser running in a Web Worker; Supabase only for optional saved fix-profiles.
why_hard_to_copy: Vendor-specific export quirks and GEDCOM 7 edge cases (extensions, EXID, GEDZIP) must be handled correctly entirely client-side.
